evidence: Read cold in 'When the adult role is not available yet': 'For that starting point, I have developed a kind of provisional bridge that I call borrowed adulthood.' then the draft 'It’s built from familiar practices like modeling and supported action, but I’m not suggesting that the whole sequence has been formally tested and proven as one treatment.' It follows straight from the sentence before: 'It' can only be the bridge / borrowed adulthood, and 'the whole sequence' looks ahead to the steps in the next paragraphs exactly as the replaced sentence's 'the steps in this process' did, so no new referent problem (C02 absent). Against the_change: both of his points are back. Familiar practices (modeling, supported action, both in his line) and only the complete sequence untested 'as one treatment' (his 'the complete sequence has been validated as one treatment'). Emulate's 'not all of the steps ... have been tested' (which implied some steps are untested) is gone. Against SOURCE: 'I’m not suggesting' and 'formally tested and proven' are the article's own words from the replaced sentence; the draft adds no claim beyond his line. His list also has witnessing and gradual transfer of responsibility, and 'like' makes the draft's two examples a partial list, not a restriction. The old announcing frame 'It is important to note here that' is dropped, which is an improvement. Tell rows, none PRESENT. Closest calls: T12 (familiar parts vs untested whole) is his own necessary concession, not a matched A/B package; T21 (two jobs in one sentence) mirrors his single line and is two clauses with no list; T01/C03 first person is his own stance ('without claiming') and does a reader-relevant job as an evidence limit; T16 is not a not-X-it's-Y; T18 the 'but' is a hedge, not a flip; T19/T11 no announcing or bridge left; T20/T29 the paragraph's last sentence adds a new consideration rather than summing up; T26 no repeated phrase; T27 no tic words; C04 the claims are his. Linter D9 'follows the source order': accepted. The draft is one sentence restoring two points in his own order, and no other order would read better; T13 is answered because the sentence draws a real distinction (parts familiar, combination untested) rather than filling a slot, and T09 does not apply to one sentence. Curly apostrophes match the section. Reads naturally in his casual voice.
